payload.claim: JARVIS bar widget (jarvis.indicator) liveness must come from the IPC socket, not systemd: probe with printf '{"command":"status"}' | socat -t 2 - UNIX-CONNECT:$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/jarvis/jarvis.sock (returns {ok,state,status,readiness} in ~0.4s; empty stdout+rc=1 when down). jarvis.service is disabled and JARVIS is normally hand-launched, so 'systemctl is-active jarvis' reports dead while it is awake.

$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/jarvis/state.json is NOT a liveness signal: assistant/ipc_service.py publish() only writes on a state transition, so its timestamp age climbs unbounded while JARVIS idles (measured 243s->268s monotonic). Use it only for descriptive fields (model/speed/latency). Also active_model is tagged ('jarvis-mini:latest') while the widget's picker keys are bare, so compare with split(':')[0].lower().

~/.config/omarchy/plugins/sathish.bar/Bar.qml had a HoverHandler referencing autohideGraceTimer, a Timer that is never defined anywhere in the plugin (and absent from stock /usr/share/omarchy/shell/plugins/bar/Bar.qml); no autohide feature exists in this bar. It threw ReferenceError on every pointer enter/leave. Fixed by reverting to stock 'onHoveredChanged: root.setBarHovered(hovered)'.

payload.test_status: verified live: icon rendered offline diamond before, then tracked idle(󱚣)/speaking(󱐋) matching concurrent socket probe JSON; journalctl --user shows 0 autohideGraceTimer and 0 JarvisIndicator errors after reload; probe returns empty+rc=1 for a dead socket so offline detection still works
